decisions.question: Where and how to tolerate extra closing braces after a complete tool-call JSON object?
decisions.choice: After json.loads and json.loads(strict=False) fail, raw_decode the first value and accept it iff it is a dict and the tail is non-empty, contains '}' and consists only of whitespace and '}'; in _loads_lenient for opencode-zen and via a local _loads_tolerant helper in core/tool_emulation.py and muse-bridge; _parse_tool_call_blocks and _normalize_arguments unchanged
alternatives: Regex-strip trailing '}' from the text before json.loads
Brace-balance repair of the raw text
Patch a raw_decode loop inside _parse_tool_call_blocks (loop does not exist in current code)
drivers: Single decode choke point per bridge
Cold path only, zero extra I/O
Negative controls ({broken, under-closed) must still return None
consequences: Over-closed envelopes now execute; counted by log line tool_call_recovered
core and muse keep their strict control-character behaviour (baseline debt, not widened)

confirmation.expected: exit 0; trailing-brace cases recovered, broken payloads still rejected in core and muse

decisions.question: How to guarantee no raw <tool_call>/<tool_invoke> block reaches client content or the next incomplete-step re-prompt, independent of the held/dedup implementation?
decisions.choice: Pure helper _strip_broken_tool_blocks(text)->(text,dropped) applied at three sinks: the ToolCallParser content sink in Handler._stream_sse (all attempts), Handler._serve_json right after _split_tool_calls, and _incomplete_tool_step_prompt; plus a one-line bridge notice when something was dropped and nothing else is visible; _is_incomplete_tool_step keeps reading raw attempt_texts so retry behaviour and caps are unchanged
alternatives: Defer and strip the held buffer until the retry decision (handoff REQ-002 literal; absent in live code, reorders the retry chain)
Add an on_unparsed callback to ToolCallParser
Change _split_tool_calls to drop unparsed blocks (breaks F-07 tests)
drivers: Baseline-neutral: works on the stale snapshot and on live
Smallest diff and same invariant for SSE and JSON
Zero leaked raw tags error budget
consequences: An unquoted unparseable tool-tag example printed by the model is dropped (RISK-002)
Scan is capped at 16 candidate tags and fails open

alternatives: Strip every closed block regardless of validity
Reject the OpenAI function wrapper as malformed
drivers: Model echoes its own history format including id
consequences: Top-level name always wins; a present-but-invalid top-level name is still rejected

Overwrite live server.py with the repo copy
